meta_skill_content: Future optimizer: prioritize recurring errors in theorem matching and claim ranking. Require a verbatim option comparison of conclusions, hypotheses, endpoints, constants, and quantifiers; rank by proven implication, not detail. An added mechanism, exception, or sharper bound is an extra claim requiring independent support—prefer the plain conclusion when it is established and the embellishment is not. In particular, guard one-sided versus two-sided estimates, O(n) versus o(n^2), and exact coefficients or cutoffs. Derive feasible valuation cases from the defining identity, including boundary values; do not assume w=0 is possible or impossible from notation alone. Preserve structural distinctions: finite maps need not separate points, and subgroups of free groups can have rank above the ambient rank. Do not infer specialized theorem facts from analogy, generic intuition, or a small numerical check. Use specializations and weight/count checks to catch transcription errors, not to certify a theorem; do not let weight agreement alone select a formula.
